classification.difficultyReason: Sketch standard sine, cosine and tangent graphs across two periods using familiar exact zeros, extrema and asymptotes; the main demand is retaining the correct branches and endpoints over the extended domain.

content.prompt: Sketch the graphs of the following in the domain $x\in[-2\pi,2\pi]$.

answer.worked: Plot the zeros at $x=-2\pi,-\pi,0,\pi,2\pi$, the maxima at $\left(-\frac{3\pi}{2},1\right)$ and $\left(\frac{\pi}{2},1\right)$, and the minima at $\left(-\frac{\pi}{2},-1\right)$ and $\left(\frac{3\pi}{2},-1\right)$. Join these points with a smooth sine curve.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5(a), answer reference on teacher PDF page 46
spec.description: Sine graph with half-pi x ticks, y ticks at plus and minus one, arrowed axes and no grid.

answer.worked: Plot the maxima at $(-2\pi,1)$, $(0,1)$ and $(2\pi,1)$, the minima at $(-\pi,-1)$ and $(\pi,-1)$, and the zeros at $x=-\frac{3\pi}{2},-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{3\pi}{2}$. Join these points with a smooth cosine curve.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5(b), answer reference on teacher PDF page 46
spec.description: Cosine graph with half-pi x ticks, y ticks at plus and minus one, arrowed axes and no grid.

answer.short: Increasing tangent branches with vertical asymptotes $x=-\frac{3\pi}{2},-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{3\pi}{2}$.
answer.worked: Mark the zeros at $x=-2\pi,-\pi,0,\pi,2\pi$ and draw dashed vertical asymptotes at $x=-\frac{3\pi}{2},-\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{3\pi}{2}$. Draw an increasing tangent branch between each pair of neighbouring asymptotes, retaining the endpoint branches.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5(c), answer reference on teacher PDF page 47
spec.description: Five visible tangent branches, four dashed asymptotes, half-pi x ticks and arrowed axes.
spec.mathematics: y=tan(x), -2pi<=x<=2pi, excluding odd multiples of pi/2
